findings.explanation: var.serviceaccount_email is wired into four distinct roles at once: the function's own runtime identity (google_cloudfunctions2_function.tf:26), the principal granted roles/cloudfunctions.invoker and roles/run.invoker on itself (google_cloudfunctions2_function_iam_member.invoker.tf:6, google_cloud_run_service_iam_member.tf:6), and the OIDC caller identity Cloud Scheduler authenticates as (google_cloud_scheduler_job.tf:15). No deterministic rule fires because each individual binding passes its own check (not allUsers, not the default Compute SA, has run.invoker as HLD_GCP_295 requires) — the issue only appears when correlating all four uses of the same variable. If the function's code is ever compromised (e.g. a dependency RCE), the attacker inherits an identity that also has self-invoke rights and is the same identity Scheduler trusts, collapsing the separation between 'who runs the code' and 'who is allowed to trigger it'. The example module (example/examplea/module.function.tf:14) confirms the pattern by passing one SA (google_service_account.scheduler) for all of these purposes.
findings.remediation: Split var.serviceaccount_email into two variables: a minimal-privilege runtime SA used only for service_config.service_account_email, and a separate caller SA used only for the IAM invoker grants and the Scheduler OIDC token. This keeps a compromised function runtime from inheriting invoke rights on itself.
findings.title: Single service account serves as function runtime identity, invoker, and Scheduler caller identity

findings.explanation: output_file_mode is explicitly set to "0666" (rw-rw-rw-), so the generated go.zip is world-writable on the machine running terraform apply between its creation and the upload performed by google_storage_bucket_object.archive. Any other local user or process on that runner can tamper with the archive's bytes before they are hashed into the object name (random_string.name keepers use filemd5 of the source path, not the zip), and the modified code would still be deployed as the Cloud Function's source. There is no holden rule for archive_file today (coverage_by_type has no entries), so this had no deterministic coverage.
findings.remediation: Drop output_file_mode (let it default per-OS) or set a non-world-writable mode such as "0600"/"0644" so only the owning build user can modify the archive before upload.
findings.title: Function source archive is built with world-writable file permissions before upload

suggested_policies.rationale: archive_file has zero existing holden coverage (coverage_by_type["archive_file"] is empty). The hashicorp/archive provider's own default for output_file_mode is the insecure "0666", and this module explicitly sets that value, so the check is concrete, broadly applicable to any Terraform using archive_file, and unambiguous: forbid world-writable octal modes on the generated build artifact.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_PROPOSED_001
name: Archive file must not be created with world-writable permissions
principle: supply-chain
severity: MEDIUM
rationale: |
  archive_file resources package local source code into a zip that is later
  uploaded as deployable artifact (e.g. Cloud Function or Lambda source). If
  output_file_mode grants write access to group or other (for example the
  provider's own default of "0666"), any other local user or process on the
  machine running terraform can tamper with the archive's contents between
  creation and upload, and the modified code will be deployed unmodified.
remediation: |
  Set output_file_mode to an owner-only-writable value, e.g.:
  ```hcl
  data "archive_file" "example" {
    output_file_mode = "0644"
  }
  ```
resources:
  archive_file:
    path: output_file_mode
    one_of: ["0644", "0600", "0640", "0444", "0400"]
